entities.text: COMMON JUDGMENT Western Coalfields Ltd. Thr. Cheif ... vs Deorao S/O Mahadeo Bobade
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard Mr. S. N. Dongre, the learned Counsel for Appellant/WCL.
None appeared for the Respondents.

2. In all these Appeals, the issue raised by the present Appellant is that the Special Tribunal, Nagpur under the Coal Bearing Areas (A & D) Act, 1957 (for short, 'the Tribunal') has committed an error by awarding interest by invoking powers under Section 17(3) of the Coal Bearing Areas (A & D) Act,
1957 (for short,'the CBA Act') vide Award dated 12/3/2010.
Hence, only to the extent of awarding interest, the Appellant had filed the present Appeals.
3. All the Appeals are arising out of same acquisition proceeding, and therefore, same can be heard and decide together by way of common Judgment.

4. In all the Appeals, it is not disputed fact that under the provisions of the CBA Act vide Notifications Section 4 dated 2/3/1985 and under Section 9 dated 10.2.1990 of the CBA Act, the residential plots/houses of village Gowari were acquired by the Appellant/WCL.

In First Appeal No.
754/2010, 4/6 75.Judg.fa.754.2010 aw connected Appeals.odt the Claimants were owners of the House/Plot No. 69, in First Appeal No. 755/2010 the Claimant was owner of the House/Plot No.
8/64 and in First Appeal No. 757/2010 the Claimants were owners of the House/Plot No. 62.
All the lands were situated at village Gowari.
In the said acquisition proceeding, after acquisition of their properties, compensation has been paid to them by the Appellant/WCL.

5. Being dissatisfied with the compensation awarded by the present Appellant, the Claimants have preferred the Application under Section 14(2) read with Section 17(2) of the CBA Act for enhancement of compensation before the Special Tribunal.

6. The Appellants have taken a stand before the Special Tribunal that the Claimants are not original owners of the properties and they are encroachers over the properties, and therefore, they are not entitled for enhancement of compensation.

In the background of this factual position, the learned Tribunal, by impugned Judgment decided the Applications filed by the respective Claimants and thereby denied the enhancement of compensation, but awarded interest on the initial amount determined by the Appellants towards compensation to them by invoking the powers under Section 17(3) of the CBA Act.

5/6 75.Judg.fa.754.2010 aw connected Appeals.odt 7. In the background of abovesaid factual position, the challenge of the Appellant before this Court is that the Claimants were not original owners of the properties which were acquired and consequently not entitled for any interest which was directed to be disbursed by the learned Tribunal and hence seeks indulgence of this Court in the matter.

8. In the present case, it is not disputed the fact that the Appellant, though came with a case that the Claimants are not original owners of the acquired land, but the Appellant had paid compensation Western Coalfields Ltd. sentences.text: During the course of argument, it is also pointed out that under the R. R. Policy, original owners of the land was also granted benefit by giving employment as also given the benefit of R. R. Policy along with compensation.

9. In the background of abovesaid factual position, it is pertinent to note that here in the present Appeal the only challenge on the part of Appellant is about awarding of the interest to the Claimants by the Tribunal.
There is no challenge on the part of Appellant to the compensation which was paid to the Claimants during the course of acquisition of the land.

Hence, in my opinion, if the Appellant is not disputing the fact that Claimants are entitled for the compensation, as a mandate of provisions of law, Respondents 6/6 75.Judg.fa.754.2010 aw connected Appeals.odt are entitled for interest for the delay caused in disbursement of amount to them.
As such, there is no error on the part of the learned Tribunal while awarding the interest on the said amount.

10. Section 17(3) of the CBA Act is very much clear that if the land is acquired and the amount of compensation is paid or deposited as required under the provisions of law, then they are liable to pay interest thereon at the rate of 5% per annum from the period when the compensation became due.

11. In the light of above facts and circumstances of the present case, as there is a mandate of Section 17(3) of the CBA Act and the same was rightly exercised by the Tribunal, I do not find any merit in all the Appeals.
The same stands dismissed.
No order as to costs.
